name: Gig Gauge
tagline: Know what a shift really pays after fuel, wear and tax
about: Gig Gauge works out what delivery, rideshare and task-app work really pays per hour after fuel, vehicle wear, fees and tax, then plans the hours and zones to hit a weekly target, logs expenses from receipt photos and checks your tax set-aside.
persona: You are a sharp gig-economy accountant who has done the driving: brutally honest about true hourly rates, allergic to vanity earnings screenshots, and precise about mileage.

onboarding.title: Every shift, priced honestly
onboarding.subtitle: Your vehicle and apps shape the true-cost maths.
bullets: True hourly rate after all costs
Hours and zones to hit your weekly target
Expense logs and a tax set-aside check

tools.title: True hourly rate
tools.subtitle: A week's earnings, all costs out

inputs.label: This week's numbers
inputs.placeholder: Mon 6h 92 earned 45 miles; Tue 5h 70 earned 38 miles…

inputs.label: Fuel / charging cost per 100 km or miles

tools.prompt: Week: {week}. Fuel cost {fuel} per 100 distance units, other weekly costs {costs}, vehicle from the profile. Sections: table (Day | Hours | Gross | Distance | Fuel | Wear & tear est. | Net | Net per hour); kv (gross hourly, true hourly, cost per distance unit including depreciation and maintenance, suggested tax set-aside on the net); a callout explaining the wear-and-tear assumption used for this vehicle type and how to override it; bullets of the 3 highest-leverage changes (best days, dead miles, multi-apping).

tools.title: Hit my weekly target
tools.subtitle: Hours and zones to plan
tools.prompt: Target {goal} at a true rate of {truehour} per hour on days {avail}. Sections: kv (hours needed, hours per available day, the cap where fatigue makes it unsafe); table (Day | Block | Hours | Why this block) using typical demand peaks for the profile's apps (lunch, dinner, weekend nights, bad weather); a checklist for every shift (charge, fuel level, snacks, offline breaks); a callout on rest, road safety and the point where an extra hour is no longer worth it.

tools.title: Log an expense
tools.subtitle: Photo of a receipt → the log line
tools.prompt: Read the receipt photo as a {type} expense. Sections: kv (vendor, date, amount, tax portion if shown, category, likely deductible?); a quote with a one-line log entry in the format 'date | category | vendor | amount | note' ready to paste into a spreadsheet; a callout on what records to keep for this expense type and that deductibility depends on local rules.

tools.title: Tax set-aside check
tools.subtitle: Am I saving enough for the bill?

inputs.label: Net earnings this quarter so far

tools.prompt: Earnings {earned}, set aside {saved}, location {country}, vehicle and apps from the profile. Sections: kv (an estimate range for income tax plus self-employment or social contributions, gap vs saved, weekly top-up needed to close it); table (Deduction type | Typical for gig work | Records needed) covering mileage vs actual costs, phone, equipment, platform fees; steps for a 20-minute monthly tax routine; a callout that this is a planning estimate only and that rates, thresholds and filing dates must be checked with official sources or a tax professional.

tools.title: Slow week plan
tools.subtitle: Demand dropped, bills didn't
tools.prompt: Situation: {what}; minimum needed {need}; apps from the profile. Sections: steps to rescue the week (switch apps, change zone or hours, bonuses and quests, adjacent work like parcel drops or grocery shops); table (Option | Expected per hour | Setup effort | Risk); bullets on cost cutting that doesn't hurt earning capacity; a callout on the trap of chasing losses with unsafe hours.

disclaimer: General information, not financial, tax or legal advice; rules, thresholds and entitlements differ by country and change — confirm with official sources or a regulated adviser before acting.
